technique: Perform parallel-bar (or ring) dips with a dip belt, vest, or carefully held dumbbell between the legs.
Keep depth in a pain-free range; load only with solid unassisted form.
setup: Secure belt; prefer parallel bars before heavy ring loading.
safety: Added load magnifies shoulder stress at end-range extension — prefer controlled depth (McKenzie et al. 2020).
contraindications: Shoulder pain; inability to perform clean unassisted dips

evidenceRefs.label: McKenzie et al. 2020 — glenohumeral extension risk considerations in the dip
McKenzie et al. 2022 — bench vs bar vs ring dip kinematics and muscle activity
de Leva 1996 — adjusted segmental mass proportions (Zatsiorsky–Seluyanov)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (technique/safety norms)

bodyweightFraction.rationale: Feet free; almost all BM is supported through the upper limbs. Hands contact the bars (~1.2% BM per de Leva male hands), so estimate ~0.96–0.99. No published GRF %BM for dips found — estimate only.
